title: Tour skips the app's only save-loop lesson
observation: Tour shows "Step 1 of 2 / Welcome to Patina" then jumps straight to "Step 2 of 2 / Your profile" (g-09, g-10). The promised middle step — "Save what you love" / "Add pieces to a room with + Add — they follow you everywhere" — never appears; the Companion intro card ("I'm your Companion.") presents immediately after (g-11).
why_it_matters: A first-time user is never taught the app's save/room-building loop before the Companion becomes the sole teacher, which then does not teach it either (its intro is a generic "I'll show you the way," not the save mechanic) — the exact mechanic T4/T5 assume the user already understands.
already_ruled: C8 correction (canon digest §6): sequencing is aspirational, not delivered; DELIVERY.md residual, unaddressed through the final hardening wave
proposal_seed: Re-anchor tour step 2 on a control that exists on the shipped Today surface, or drop the step and its promise together.

title: Coach-mark buttons use the app's only system blue
observation: "Skip" and "Next"/"Done" render in iOS system blue (#007AFF) on both tour steps (g-09, g-10) — the only blue anywhere in an app whose entire palette is cream/charcoal/mocha/clay.
why_it_matters: The very first interactive controls a new user sees break the brand system before the user has seen anything else to compare it to, undermining the "considered, unhurried" first impression the rest of the screen (Playfair serif, warm tan) is built to give.
proposal_seed: Style the tour's Skip/Next/Done as PatinaButton .ghost/.secondary, not system-default blue text buttons.

title: Coach-mark bubble hides the element it describes
observation: Tour step 1's bubble ("This is your Daily Room — picks and stories chosen for your space.") is a full-width opaque card that sits directly over the Next Move card it is explaining (g-09) — only the card's trailing arrow icon peeks out past the bubble's edge.
why_it_matters: A teaching moment that occludes its own subject teaches nothing; the user has to dismiss the coach mark before they can see what it was pointing at, breaking the explain-then-look sequence the tour exists for.
proposal_seed: Position the tour bubble below or beside its anchor with a visible pointer, never on top of it.

title: Browse grid renders off-canvas, unreadable cards
observation: "Browse pieces / 10 pieces curated for your space" (g-15): the left column's card is cropped by the screen edge — its title reads "...M & BOARD" / "...rloom Oak" / "...ing Table" / ",200" with no left half visible — while the right column's card is a normal full 46%-match chair card. Under the "Seating" filter (g-16) three cards of visibly different heights overlap each other, and the third card renders as a flat brown gradient tile with no product image at all.
why_it_matters: This is the app's only browse surface for every category and every tier (T3's whole task), and it is illegible on the side that matters most (price, name) for roughly half the grid on first load.
proposal_seed: Give both grid columns one fixed card width/height and clip images to it; stop free-sizing card content.

title: No search exists anywhere in the app
observation: The task "Find a sofa for our living room" has no search field to answer it with. The shortest real path is Companion orb → "Your recommendations" → chip "Seating" (client-side filter over an already-fetched ≤20-row page) → card — 4 acts, and it is a filtered browse, not a search.
why_it_matters: A shopper who already knows what they want ("a sofa") is forced through an untargeted feed instead of typing the word — the single highest-intent entry to the commerce surface is missing.
proposal_seed: Add a search field to Browse pieces that queries the catalog server-side, not just the current filter chips.

title: Filter chips imply catalog-wide scope but only filter one loaded page
observation: Tapping "Seating" changes the subtitle to "3 pieces curated for your space" (g-16), reading as if the catalog holds only 3 seating pieces — the chips filter the same ≤20 rows already on screen; the RPC's `p_category` parameter is never sent.
why_it_matters: A shopper comparing sofas sees a near-empty result (3 items, one of them a blank gradient tile) and reasonably concludes Patina doesn't carry much seating, when the constraint is a client-side filter, not real inventory.
proposal_seed: Send p_category to get_recommendations on chip tap so counts reflect the real catalog, not the current page.

title: Piece detail is a dead end with no bespoke exit
observation: Every product tapped from Browse renders only "Couldn't load product" / "Let's try that again" (g-17). There is no back chevron, no nav, and (per the accessibility tree the walkers report) the Companion is absent from this screen entirely — the only element on it is the retry link, and retry fails identically. Reproduces identically in dark (d-04) and at XXL Dynamic Type (x-04).
why_it_matters: ProductDetailView is deliberately exempt from the shared PatinaScreenChrome back button because it owns a bespoke floating exit (C19) — but that bespoke exit only exists in the success layout; in the one state every real tap currently lands in, it never renders, so the screen's one designed way out is the one state that has none.
already_ruled: C19 (screen-chrome exemption is deliberate for the success state; this finding is about the error state having no exit of its own, not about the exemption itself)
proposal_seed: Render a back chevron in the error state layout too, independent of whether the product payload loaded.

title: Product photography does not match the listed piece
observation: "Heirloom Oak Dining Table" (Room & Board) shows a table with green velvet chairs, not oak; "Live-Edge Coffee Table" (Lee Industries) shows an old wooden ladder-back chair on grass, not a coffee table (g-15).
why_it_matters: On a marketplace whose brand pitch is provenance and honest materials, a photo that doesn't match the piece is the fastest way to lose trust before price or maker even register.
proposal_seed: Add an image-to-product integrity check to the seed/catalog pipeline before this ships past local seed data.

title: Saved opens on a tab that says nothing is saved
observation: "Saved" opens on the "Boards" tab by default, reading "No boards yet" / "Save pieces from recommendations to create your first board" (g-21) — for an account that has one real saved item sitting one tap away under "All items" (g-22b).
why_it_matters: T4's whole premise is "find it again tomorrow" — the surface built for exactly that opens on an empty-looking screen even when the thing you're looking for is there, one tab over.
proposal_seed: Default Saved to whichever tab is non-empty, or to "All items" until a board actually holds something.

title: "Create Board" is the primary CTA on a dead-end feature
observation: The empty Boards tab's only action is a full-width black "Create Board" button (g-21). Nothing in the app can ever add a piece to a board once created.
why_it_matters: The one call to action offered on the surface built for return-investment leads to a feature that can never do the thing its own copy describes ("create your first board") — a user who follows the CTA gets a permanently empty container.
proposal_seed: Either wire addToBoard to a real call site (a card's ⋯ menu "Add to board") or remove the Create Board CTA until it does something.

title: The nav row back to Saved can vanish for the exact saves the app invites
observation: The Companion's "Saved" row only appears when tableItemCount > 0, and tableItemCount counts only room-scoped SavedItems (not the TableItemModel rows the piece-detail heart or an unscoped browse-card save actually creates). Saved has no other door anywhere in the app (per code read; the Companion is the sole nav surface, T13).
why_it_matters: "Find it again tomorrow" (T4) depends on a nav row that is architecturally invisible for the two most obvious ways to save a piece — heart on the detail screen, heart on an unscoped browse card — meaning a user who saves the way the UI most directly invites them to has no path back to Saved at all.
proposal_seed: Count all TableItemModel rows for the Companion's Saved-row gate, not only room-scoped SavedItems.

title: Price format changes between the grid and Saved
observation: The same piece prices as "$4,200" on the browse grid and "$4200" (no thousands separator) on its Saved row (g-22b).
why_it_matters: A price that reformats between two screens showing the same number reads as a small crack in an app asking someone to trust a four-figure purchase decision.
proposal_seed: Route both surfaces through the same currency formatter.

title: A 6-point-wide toggle silently corrupts room data
observation: The "ft / m" unit toggle (g-25) renders "ft" at roughly 12×13pt and "m" at roughly 6×13pt — well under the 44pt minimum. Typing 18/14 with the toggle mis-hit on "m" produces no visible state change ("ft" stays bold) but silently reinterprets the entry as metres, yielding a "Living Room" of 59'×46' = 2713 sq ft, which then persists to the room view, the home Active Room card, and Profile.
why_it_matters: T5's whole premise is the room as "the object of return" — a 6-point touch target with zero feedback on activation is the root cause of a corrupted room object that then contaminates every downstream screen for the rest of the account's life.
proposal_seed: Make ft/m a 44pt segmented control with a visible selected state; recompute (not reinterpret) already-typed values on toggle.

title: Room stats show undefined abbreviations
observation: The room's stat row reads "0 ITEMS", "— MATCH", "0 IN AR" with no legend anywhere on screen (g-28b, c-24, d-06). "IN AR" never has a value other than 0 for any room, on any account, because no product in the catalog has a usdz model.
why_it_matters: A stat that is permanently 0 and never explained reads as either broken or meaningless the first time it's noticed, and it is always the former — the AR pipeline literally cannot produce a nonzero count today.
proposal_seed: Drop the "In AR" stat until usdz models exist for at least one product, and label "Match" with what it's matching against.

title: One action is offered under three different names, stacked
observation: The empty room's body copy reads "We've already found pieces that would fit this space. Browse your Daily Room to start building this room.", directly above a button labeled "Browse Picks for This Room", directly above a link labeled "SEE RECOMMENDATIONS →" (g-28b, c-24, d-06) — three different phrasings stacked for what appears to be one underlying destination.
why_it_matters: Three labels for one act make the user pause to work out whether they're different options before tapping any of them — the opposite of the "success looks like" bar T5 sets (piece lands in the room without hunting).
proposal_seed: Cut to one CTA with one label; drop the body-copy restatement and the redundant link.

surface: Browse grid card menu, room context
title: There is no "Add to room" action, even entered from the room itself
observation: Even when the browse grid is entered from a room's own "Browse Picks for This Room" CTA, the card's ⋯ menu still offers only "Save / Share / Not for me / View details" — no room-add action exists anywhere in that menu.
why_it_matters: The room view's own copy promises "start building this room," but the mechanism it points to (browse, then the card menu) never offers a way to actually put anything into the room — the loop the app's own words describe does not exist.
proposal_seed: Add "Add to this room" to the card ⋯ menu when the grid was entered with a room context.

title: AR is offered by the UI but cannot ever render
observation: The room stat row's "0 IN AR" (g-28b, c-24, d-06) is not a display bug — usdz_url is NULL::text in the recommendation RPC and hard-coded nil in the direct product fetch, so product.hasARModel is false on every code path in the app; the AR button never draws on any piece, for any account.
why_it_matters: "See it in my room" (T5) has an AR door that the UI implies exists (a stat that counts it, a Companion row named "Try in your room") but that door leads nowhere for every single product in the catalog — this is a server-contract fact, not a Simulator limitation, so it is not a device-owed unknown.
proposal_seed: Suppress every AR-shaped affordance (button, stat, Companion row) until at least one product carries a real usdz_url.

title: The only door to the Studio is the worst-reached control on the screen
observation: The three top-right glyphs (bell, ?, monogram) sit as ~36pt targets in the far top-right corner (g-12, x-01) — the single hardest zone to reach one-handed on a phone this size — and the monogram is the sole door to Profile → Studio, the surface holding every project/proposal/invoice/decision the app knows about.
why_it_matters: The Companion orb (the app's best-placed control, per its own 120pt bottom hearth) can reach almost everything else in the app in one tap; the one thing it structurally cannot reach for an activeProject client without a detour is the Studio, which sits behind the one control placed for the least reachable hand position.
proposal_seed: Add a Studio door to the Companion panel's universal tail, or move the monogram into the bottom hearth's reach zone.

title: The status bar draws over scrolled content, worst on modal sheets at XXL
observation: In dark mode, the fixed status bar (9:41, signal icons) draws over the scrolled Studio list — the clock sits directly on "Review by Sep 8" (d-02). At XXL Dynamic Type the Dynamic-Island pill itself, not just the clock digits, occludes the top proposal's title (x-02). A third reproduction lands on a modal sheet: the "Your design request" sheet's own "Close" button and title overlap the 9:41 clock at XXL (x-06).
why_it_matters: This is a systemic missing safe-area inset, not one screen's bug — it reproduces on a plain list, on the same list at a different type size, and on a completely different component (a sheet), which means any new scrollable surface is likely to inherit it.
proposal_seed: Audit every scrolled list and sheet header for a top safe-area inset; this looks like one shared layout omission, not several.

title: One screen ignores the dark-mode override entirely
observation: With the system/app appearance set to dark for the whole walk (confirmed by every surrounding shot: d-01, d-02, d-06, d-07, d-08, d-09, d-10 all render dark), the room-summary step "Here's what I see" (d-06a) renders in the app's light theme — cream ground, near-black text — sitting between two dark screens in the same unbroken session.
why_it_matters: A user who set dark mode for eye comfort (bus, night, whatever the reason) gets one jarring bright screen mid-flow with no warning, and it is exactly the screen showing them the corrupted room dimensions (U2-13) — the two defects compound on the same screen.
proposal_seed: Route the room-summary screen through the same dynamic color tokens as the rest of the room flow.

title: The filter chip row overflows the screen at XXL with no way to reach the last chip
observation: At Dynamic Type XXL, the chip row (All / Seating / Tables / Lighting / Storage) runs off the right edge — "Storage" is clipped to "Stor" with no visible scroll indicator or affordance suggesting more chips exist (x-03).
why_it_matters: A user on the accessibility text size this row was supposedly built to survive (per the code's own accessibility-size branches elsewhere) cannot select the Storage filter at all — the control is present but physically unreachable.
proposal_seed: Wrap the chip row or make it a horizontally scrolling ScrollView with a fade/arrow hint at XXL.

title: Body text runs into the Companion button with no reserved space
observation: At XXL, the "Space Plan" section's wrapped body text ("Conversation seating around the fireplace,...") is cut off directly by the fixed circular Companion button at the screen's bottom edge, with no bottom padding reserved for it (x-05).
why_it_matters: The Companion hearth is described elsewhere as "reserved layout space, not a persistent visible bar" — here it behaves like neither: it isn't reserved (content runs under it) and it isn't avoided (it clips the last visible line), the worst of both.
proposal_seed: Give scrollable content a bottom inset equal to the Companion hearth's height at every Dynamic Type size.

title: Home doesn't scroll, and gives no sign anything is hidden
observation: For the activeProject account (3 projects, 4 proposals, 1 open invoice, 2 pending decisions), d-01 (top) and d-02 (after a swipe) are pixel-identical — the screen has no more content to reveal, so the swipe simply does nothing.
why_it_matters: A screen with real, current, dollar-figure work waiting (T13's "one-handed on the bus" reader would want exactly this) offers no scroll cue, no "more below" affordance, and no indication that four pending items exist two acts away behind the monogram — it just ends.
proposal_seed: If Today truly has nothing more to show, say so; if the Studio surface should be reachable from here, mount it.

title: "Account >" is a fully-styled dead row
observation: Settings' ACCOUNT section shows an "Account" row with an icon and a chevron (g-02b); tapping dead-centre of its frame changes nothing on screen — no push, no sheet, no feedback. Reproduces identically for a guest and a signed-in client.
why_it_matters: A row drawn exactly like every other navigable row in the same list, that silently does nothing, teaches the user their taps in this app might just not work — a trust cost that's cheap to avoid.
proposal_seed: Either build the Account screen or remove the row until it does.

title: There is no Sign Out control anywhere in the app
observation: Neither Settings nor Profile carries a Sign Out action for a signed-in client. The only way to end a session is to force-quit and wipe the device keychain from outside the app — not performable by an end user.
why_it_matters: Switching or removing an account is table-stakes account-management, and its total absence blocks the household scenario T12 depends on (a second person on the same phone) as much as it blocks simple account hygiene.
proposal_seed: Add Sign Out to Settings (the working AccountView code already has the alert copy written — it just has no live door to it, per the Account-row finding above).

title: Two different quizzes exist for one concept and disagree with each other
observation: The Companion-entry quiz's first question ("Which palette feels like home?", g-06) offers Warm Minimal / Cool Modern / Classic Comfort / Eclectic Curated. The quiz reached after manually entering a room ("Which room speaks to you?", g-26) offers Warm Minimal / Cool Modern / Layered Comfort / Curated Mix — two of four options differ, for what the app treats as the same StylePreferenceModel.
why_it_matters: A user who takes both (easy to do, since the room-creation flow surfaces its own quiz unprompted) gets two different taste labels for one underlying preference, with no indication either quiz knows the other exists.
proposal_seed: Collapse to one quiz asset reused by both entry points, or make the second entry point resume the first quiz's answers instead of re-asking.

title: "YOUR ROOM IS CAPTURED" mislabels a typed form
observation: After completing the manual (typed) room-entry form, the very next screen's eyebrow reads "YOUR ROOM IS CAPTURED · LET'S DISCOVER YOUR STYLE" (g-26) — no camera or scan of any kind occurred; the user typed length, width, window and door counts into text fields.
why_it_matters: "Captured" implies a photographic or spatial scan happened; claiming it for a typed form is the same class of overstatement the brand-voice rules exist to prevent (no fabricated capability claims), and it sets a false expectation for what data the app actually has about the room.
proposal_seed: Use language that's honest about the entry method, e.g. "Your room is saved" for the manual-entry fork.

surface: AuthScreenView presented as a mid-flow sheet
title: The design-request soft wall removes every escape hatch the real gate has
observation: The generic auth gate (g-02, s-01) offers Sign in with Apple, Continue with Google, Continue with email, and "Look around first." The same screen thrown mid-flow as a soft wall after "Send request" (g-35) is missing "Look around first" and has no Cancel or X anywhere — only a blind downward drag dismisses it, and nothing on the sheet mentions the request that triggered it.
why_it_matters: A first-time guest who just finished a multi-step design request hits a wall with strictly fewer exits than the app's own front door, at the exact moment they're most likely to feel trapped rather than invited to sign in.
proposal_seed: Give the soft-wall variant of AuthSheet an explicit Cancel/X, and name the thing it's gating ("Sign in to send your request").

title: The Companion's own headline changes wording for the same panel
observation: The identical "where next" panel is titled "Where to begin?" for a 0-room guest (g-14b) and "Where to next?" for a 1-room activeProject client (d-09, x-09) — two headlines for what is functionally the same menu of Companion rows.
why_it_matters: Minor on its own, but it's one more instance of the app not having a single stable name for a recurring piece of UI — the same pattern this program's grounding already flags for the designer-help CTA and the taste-portrait label; small inconsistencies like this compound into an app that reads as less considered than its visual design promises.
proposal_seed: This one may be intentional (0 rooms vs. 1+ rooms) — worth a ruling either way rather than an unreviewed drift.
